risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: too_harsh: system GMM with lagged income and an external instrument (ICT goods imports) is a strategy, weak (30 instruments vs 24 countries, exclusion arguable) but not 'none', so moderate fits the guide better than serious.
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: agree: ad hoc weighted composite with overlapping components and a Table 1 definition error (internet users defined via mobile broadband), moderate.
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: agree: 24 Asian economies by data availability, short panel (216 obs), inconsistent i=1..11 notation, moderate.
risk_of_bias.outcome_measurement: too_harsh: log PPP GDP per capita from WDI is a standard measure (defined in Table 1); only the GNI/GDI labelling is inconsistent, so low-to-moderate.
risk_of_bias.specification: agree: single model, undocumented instrument choices, no sensitivity to instrument count; HDI in abstract but absent from Table 4, moderate.
risk_of_bias.selective_reporting: agree: only one model shown, ICTSERS not estimated, some textual misreadings of the table (constant called initial condition; trade sign), moderate.
risk_of_bias.why: Same system-GMM design as paper 323 (rated moderate on confounding there); under the guide a standard dynamic panel with an external instrument but unestablished exogeneity is moderate. Instrument proliferation and several interpretation slips push it to the upper end, so serious is borderline rather than clearly warranted.

problems: Core numbers in the record match Table 4. risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: agree: causal verbs ('effect', 'impact', 'engender'), levels regressions, headline FGLS without country or year effects, no handling of reverse causation.
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: agree: standard World Bank internet and mobile series; mobile subscriptions are SIM counts (max 198 per 100), moderate.
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: agree: 20 countries built around two focal cases, 'selected at random' with no sampling frame; borderline serious/moderate.

risk_of_bias.why: Cross-sectional levels regressions with causal language, no strategy for reverse causality, and a poorly constructed small sample with misread interactions; serious is appropriate.

problems: Numerical entries in the record match Tables III-V. eligibility_note: Own DEA/Malmquist decomposition and regressions on 24 OECD economies (>=10), ICT capital stock as exposure, labour productivity as output outcome. Eligible, though the main result is an accounting decomposition without standard errors.

results.correction: Sect. 4.2, p.138-139 (Fig. 2). No standard error, N or controls are reported for any of the three regressions.

Numbers are right (Tn=0.772, bootstrap p=0.108), but the direction should be null/inconclusive rather than positive: it is a non-rejection of equality between the 2019 distribution and the 1995 distribution scaled by DACC, not a positive estimate. Non-rejection also occurs for EFF alone (p=0.093) and for several other combinations, so the test does not isolate ICT. The authors' 'ICT capital contributes to convergence' is an interpretation of the counterfactual and Fig. 3.

risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: agree: accounting decomposition and bivariate regressions with no controls or instruments, yet abstract speaks of 'positive impact'; reverse causation ignored.
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: too_lenient: ICT capital stock per hour is a direct measure, but DACC is a model-derived counterfactual component, the paper itself notes spending shifting from ICT assets to services (not captured), and falling constant-price ICT stock in 12 countries suggests deflation/measurement issues; moderate fits better.
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: agree: 24 OECD economies, mostly high income, moderate.
risk_of_bias.outcome_measurement: agree: GDP per hour worked from OECD with PPP and 2015 prices.
risk_of_bias.specification: agree: deterministic DEA, CRS, no technological regress, no standard errors on the decomposition, regression N and form unreported; moderate.
risk_of_bias.selective_reporting: agree: all 24 countries, all 15 distribution tests and a 4-year robustness check are shown; regression details (N, SE) omitted but minor.
risk_of_bias.why: Descriptive accounting with unadjusted regressions and causal wording, no handling of reverse causality; serious is appropriate for causal claims, though the decomposition itself is transparent.

problems: No invented numbers found. Points to correct: (a) result 7 direction; (b) the record's claim that regressions 'use few observations' cannot be verified, since the paper reports no N or SE for the Fig. 1-2 regressions; (c) the abstract's 'positive impact' and 'contributes to convergence' go beyond what a non-causal decomposition and a non-rejection test support; (d) record exposure description 'ICT capital stock per hour worked' matches the paper's d = D/L normalisation.

risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: agree: system GMM with lagged TFP and an external ICT-import instrument is a strategy, weak diagnostics (29 instruments vs 24 countries, Hansen p=0.935); moderate.
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: agree: undocumented composite index, interaction without main effect; moderate.

risk_of_bias.outcome_measurement: agree: TFP as an undocumented residual (alpha and capital measure unreported, units absent); moderate and close to serious for replicability.

problems: Record matches the text and Table 5; its inconsistency list (HDI, 10% vs p=0.000, C-test 0.222 vs 0.822, 240 vs 216) is correct, as are the missing-table observation (tables numbered 2, 3, 5). Additional points: (a) same authors, same 24-country 2000-2010 sample and same ICTMI/ICTSERT setup as paper 302, so not independent evidence; (b) the text calls the AR(1) p=0.077 acceptable but AR(1) is expected to reject; (c) the Fig. 1 'ICT Augmented Convergence Hypothesis' diagram is carried over from 302 and does not match this paper's TFP model.
